title: ‘Liar! Liar! Pants on Fire!’
main_content:
“Liar, liar, pants on fire!”

Children all over the United States know this simple rhyme. They say it when someone gets caught in a lie.

The word “lie” comes from Old English through even older German. A lie is an untruth. It is intentional and usually has consequences.

But not all lies are created equal.

People often use white lies to prevent hurting the feelings of others. For example, let’s say you are eating dinner at your boss’s house and the food is really bad. When your boss asks you, “How do you like the meatloaf? It’s an old family recipe,” it is a good idea to say you love it.

Another kind of relatively harmless lies is called a fib. It is a little, unimportant lie. Fibbers who fib are usually not out to hurt anyone.

Sometimes people simply make things up. Other times they stretch the truth, or exaggerate. In other words, they add details to the truth to make a story better.

questions.question: What are fibs?
options: Deliberate attempts to deceive for personal gain
Small, unimportant lies that are not intended to harm
Major untruths that can result in serious consequences
questions.answer: Small, unimportant lies that are not intended to harm

questions.question: When can you use “Liar, liar, pants on fire!”?
options: When someone gets caught in a lie
When someone is being very truthful
When someone is playing a game
questions.answer: When someone gets caught in a lie

questions.question: Why do people say white lies?
options: To prevent hurting the feelings of others
questions.answer: To prevent hurting the feelings of others
